classification: CURRENT OWNER columns are CURRENT_FACT, verified against app/ on 2026-09-26. DOMAIN OWNER / CREATIVE OWNER / SHARED columns are RECOMMENDATION. Where ownership cannot be determined from evidence it is OPEN_DECISION.
status: PROPOSAL ONLY. Nothing was moved, created, renamed or deleted. This matrix assigns ownership; it does not implement it.
purpose: Answers, for every capability a Creative Marketplace touches: who owns the domain rule today, who must own it in the target, whether the capability is shared or Creative-only, and which layer owns the database, the application orchestration and the infrastructure. Its purpose is to make double-ownership and accidental ownership impossible to go unnoticed.

ownership_rule.statement: Every new class must have exactly one clear domain owner (AGENTS.md section 7). A capability that has two domain owners is a defect, not a shared service. Sharing happens through a contract, never through a shared entity.
ownership_rule.consequence_for_creative: Creative owns Creative aggregates. It does not own identity, storage, payments, FX, notifications, audit, configuration or geography, and it does not co-own them either.

shared_versus_creative_rule.statement: A capability is SHARED when Creative consumes the identical rule for the identical reason. A capability is CREATIVE when the rule exists only because Creative exists. A capability is BORROWED-PATTERN when Creative must build its own because the existing rule is advertising-specific. These three cases require three different designs and conflating them is the primary risk in this initiative.

ownership_conflicts_identified.detail: In this repository 'Asset' means advertising inventory (screens, screen_categories, coverage tables). A developer searching for Creative assets will find screens and booking_media first.

resolution.statement: Creative names its file aggregate CreativeFile. The term 'Asset' is not used for Creative work anywhere in code, schema or documentation.

ownership_conflicts_identified.detail: booking_media.review_status is an ADMIN MODERATION of client-uploaded advertisement files. A Creative client review of creator work is a different thing entirely.

resolution.statement: Creative uses CreativeReview / creative_reviews. Moderation is a separate concern and is not reused.

ownership_conflicts_identified.detail: testimonials is public marketing content with a rating column, no author binding and no soft delete.

resolution.statement: Creative reviews are never written to testimonials. See artifact 10, highest-risk list rank 2.

ownership_conflicts_identified.detail: partners is an affiliate organisation with referral and commission terms; a creator is an individual supplier of creative work.

resolution.statement: Separate aggregate. Do not model a creator as a partner 'because one already exists'.

ownership_conflicts_identified.detail: reward_accounts / reward_transactions are an integer points ledger tied to bookings. Creator earnings are money.

resolution.statement: Reuse the SHAPE (account + append-only entries + lifetime counters) with decimal(12,2) and a currency column. Never the integer representation.

single_owner_assertions.statement: Capabilities Creative must NOT own, restated as a single-owner check for review: Authentication, Users, Media inventory, Storage disks, Payment gateway, Currency/FX, Notification delivery, Settings store, Audit store, Geography reference. If a Creative class writes to any of these stores directly, it has crossed the boundary.
capabilities_creative_does_own: Project and its frozen agreed terms

discrepancies_vs_existing_artifacts.topic: Phase 0.20 documentation claims app/Domain/Creative, app/Services/Creative, app/Repositories/Creative and app/Http/Controllers/Creative were CREATED (empty).
discrepancies_vs_existing_artifacts.resolution: False. Verified absent on 2026-09-26. Recorded as a documentation discrepancy in AGENTS.md section 8 and in docs/audit/creative-marketplace/. The absence is the reason the whole Creative capability column above reads NONE.

discrepancies_vs_existing_artifacts.topic: Earlier artifacts state 74 tables / 94 foreign keys (AGENTS.md baseline).
discrepancies_vs_existing_artifacts.resolution: Measured 73 distinct tables and 96 foreign-key definitions (94 ->constrained() + 2 legacy ->foreign()) from the 112 migrations. Source wins; recorded as baseline drift, not a schema change.

safety_statement.statement: Producing this matrix changed no production code, no migration, no model, no route and no test. It asserts ownership; it does not move anything. Any relocation implied here is a separate, explicitly authorised task that must satisfy AGENTS.md section 15 (inventory -> classify -> identify consumers -> move -> update namespace -> update imports -> update bindings -> resolve consumers -> verify container -> run tests).
